messages:
Priya (PM): quick sync — need to finalize enterprise audit + BYOK priorities for next quarter. three customer blockers. can we get clear launch criteria and rough estimates?
Matt (Eng): can you list the concrete acceptance criteria we should design to? eg what does 'BYOK ready' mean for legal & infra.
Maya (CS): fwiw customers: A requires BYOK before onboarding (enterprise telco), B needs 7yr exportable audit history (finance), C just wants legal-hold APIs. BYOK is the gating ask for A.
Ken (Security): must-haves from security: tamper-evident audit entries, immutable retention window for exported data, signed attestations for BYOK handshake, and KMS policies for rotation. also document threat model for escrow.
Diego (Eng Infra): storage/ops note — full raw audit logs for 7yrs is heavy. recommend export-first model: short-term hot index + on-demand export to customer S3. we can offer both but need cost model.
Eli (SRE): fallback plan: if customer BYOK handshake fails at deploy, fallback to shared customer-key with explicit audit event and opt-in. but legal customers likely reject fallback. canary is required.
Priya (PM): proposed priority: 1) BYOK per-tenant handshake + attestation artifact 2) Audit export API (S3-delivery, incremental) 3) Legal-hold API + UI + retention freeze. Need security sign-off, SOC2 control mapping, e2e tests, and runbook for launch.
Matt (Eng): rough staffing estimates: BYOK handshake + attestation ~ 4w eng + 2w infra + 1w QA. Audit export API ~ 2w eng + 1w infra. Legal-hold primitives ~ 1w eng + 1w product/UX. these are high-level.
Ken (Security): acceptance checklist we expect before sign-off:
- BYOK: handshake API + attestation blob (verifiable, signed)
- BYOK: KMS policy enforcement and rotation detection alerts
- Audit: immutable append-only store for 90d + export pipeline for long-term archive
- Legal-hold: freeze flag + tamper-evident release log
- SOC2: map controls to evidence artifacts (exportable bundle)

Diego (Eng Infra): sample API sketch for export & BYOK handshake — pls bikeshed: 
```
POST /v1/tenants/{tid}/byok/handshake
{ "key_uri": "kms://aws/arn:...", "approver": "legal@cust.com" }
-> 202 accepted + attestation: base64(ecdsa-sign(...))

GET /v1/tenants/{tid}/audit/export?start=...&end=...&dest=s3://bucket/path
-> 200 queued; returns job_id
```

Maya (CS): +1 to canary list. propose customers A + small B pilot. Maya will coordinate acceptance tests and legal checklist with them.
Evan (Legal): legal-hold requirements: API must record issuer, reason, and immutable timestamp; only authorized roles can release. for BYOK we need an auditable proof-of-control and explicit escrow terms if we hold keys. add DSAR (data subject) handling to runbook.
Matt (Eng): open questions: do we require HSM-backed key material for BYOK first pass or allow customer-managed KMS URIs (no escrow) as v1? HSM gives stronger claim for SOC2 but costs time.
Ken (Security): v1 can accept customer KMS URIs (no escrow) but we must surface attestation + proof-of-ownership. HSM-only could be v2.
Eli (SRE): rollout plan: canary to 2 customers behind feature-flag, monitor latency and export job saturation, then 10-customers, then GA. include automatic fallback path and ops playbook.
Priya (PM): action items: Matt + Diego to produce detailed eng estimates and API contract by EOD Thu; Ken + Evan to produce security + legal acceptance checklist by Fri; Maya to confirm pilot customers and test criteria. schedule 45m follow-up Monday to lock roadmap. @Maya please add canary list. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduled meeting created: Mon 10:00 — "Enterprise audit/BYOK roadmap sync"
Matt (Eng): noted — will start a design doc and tag folks.
Maya (CS): adding pilot customers now.
Ken (Security): will draft checklist and include example attestation format.
Evan (Legal): will draft required contract language for escrow & acceptance clauses.
Priya (PM): thanks — we'll aim to ship BYOK handshake + attestations in Q2 canary, audit export + legal-hold shortly after.
